2609.24324.title: Brain-Token Learning: Microstate-Based Tokenization and Multi-Scale Interaction for Long-Horizon EEG Sequence Modeling
2609.24324.paper_summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive window into dynamic brain activity, yet modeling long-horizon EEG sequences remains challenging due to their high temporal complexity, substantial variability across subjects, and the lack of biologically meaningful sequence representations. Existing tokenization strategies, such as fixed-window and patch-based representations, discretize EEG signals according to artificial temporal boundaries, which may disrupt intrinsic brain-state dynamics. In this work, we propose Brain-Token Learning, a neuroscience-inspired framework that introduces Brain Tokenization for long-horizon EEG sequence modeling. Instead of partitioning EEG signals into predefined temporal segments, Brain Tokenization represents EEG as sequences of recurrent microstate-derived brain tokens, where each token corresponds to a quasi-stable large-scale brain state with variable temporal duration. Based on these biologically grounded tokens, we further develop a multi-scale token interaction module consisting of Latent State Aggregation and State Transition Modeling to jointly capture global brain-state context and local microstate transitions. We evaluate Brain-Token on five heterogeneous EEG datasets, including the newly collected long-horizon NeuroLong dataset and four affective or clinical EEG datasets (SEED, DEAP, MDD, and NSSI). Extensive experiments demonstrate that Brain-Token consistently outperforms conventional CNN/LSTM architectures, Transformer-based models, and domain adaptation methods across diverse EEG scenarios. Further analysis verifies the effectiveness of microstate-based tokenization and multi-scale interaction for learning robust and interpretable EEG representations. These results establish Brain-Token as a biologically grounded tokenization paradigm for long-horizon EEG sequence modeling.
2609.24324.paper_summary_zh: 腦電圖 (EEG) 提供了一個非侵入性的窗口來觀察動態腦活動，但由於其高時間複雜性、受試者之間的顯著變異性以及缺乏生物學上有意義的序列表示，建模長期 EEG 序列仍然具有挑戰性。現有的標記化策略，如固定窗口和基於區塊的表示，根據人工時間邊界對 EEG 信號進行離散化，這可能會破壞內在的腦狀態動態。在這項工作中，我們提出了腦標記學習，這是一個受神經科學啟發的框架，引入了腦標記化以進行長期 EEG 序列建模。腦標記化不是將 EEG 信號劃分為預定的時間段，而是將 EEG 表示為由重複微狀態衍生的腦標記序列，其中每個標記對應於一個具有可變時間持續性的準穩定大規模腦狀態。基於這些生物學上基礎的標記，我們進一步開發了一個多尺度標記互動模塊，包含潛在狀態聚合和狀態轉移建模，以共同捕捉全局腦狀態上下文和局部微狀態轉移。我們在五個異質 EEG 數據集上評估了腦標記，包括新收集的長期 NeuroLong 數據集和四個情感或臨床 EEG 數據集（SEED、DEAP、MDD 和 NSSI）。廣泛的實驗表明，腦標記在各種 EEG 場景中始終優於傳統的 CNN/LSTM 架構、基於Transformer的模型和領域適應方法。進一步的分析驗證了基於微狀態的標記化和多尺度互動在學習穩健且可解釋的 EEG 表示方面的有效性。這些結果確立了腦標記作為一種生物學上基礎的標記化範式，用於長期 EEG 序列建模。
